endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Define criteria for which documents or records are eligible/ineligible for inclusion in the retrieval corpus (e.g., only verified clinical guidelines, only records from defined date ranges).

evidence.title: Why Trust Your Agent? Empirical Security Gains from TRiSM-Guided Agentic Workflows in Healthcare
evidence.effect: Least-privilege, defence-in-depth workflows improved security and accuracy; attack success fell 31% to 10% and 42% to 25%, and accuracy rose 72.5% to 86.5%.
evidence.quote: This paper contributes to knowledge by demonstrating least-privilege, defence in depth agentic workflows improving security and accuracy, while also highlighting model choice is a necessary architectural consideration.

evidence.title: SkinAgent AI: A Safety-Grounded Multimodal Agentic Framework for Non-Diagnostic Skincare Support
evidence.outcome: Cross-user data leakage and safety/privacy violations in finite test suites
evidence.effect: No violations or successful cross-user leakage events were observed in the finite safety and privacy test suites.
evidence.quote: No violations or successful cross-user leakage events were observed in the finite safety and privacy test suites.

commentary.bottom_line: One simulated benchmark found that least-privilege, defence-in-depth agent workflows lowered attack success from 31% to 10% and from 42% to 25% and raised accuracy from 72.5% to 86.5%, but no study tested isolated environments or governance of persistent memory and retention in clinical settings. The recommendation rests on a single framework endorsement and indirect, offline evidence.

perspectives.view: The only test of the practice (arxiv:2606.28666) is a level 5 automated benchmark with 800 report generations and 500 attack scenarios run offline. Its results favor least privilege, but indirectness, a single study, and no patient or clinical outcomes lower certainty to very low. The memory retention and access-control component has no test at all.

Attack success fell from 31% to 10% and from 42% to 25% under restricted workflows, which suggests fewer paths for an agent to reach data outside its task. A separate benchmark (arxiv:2609.29341) observed no cross-user leakage in 240 cases, but finite test suites cannot show that leakage never occurs, and that study did not test the safeguard.

Both studies ran in simulated environments, so they say nothing about how least-privilege scoping, sandboxing, or memory retention rules perform inside live EHR integrations. The accuracy gain from 72.5% to 86.5% may not carry over once agents face real permission models, credential management, and clinician workflows.

The CHAI playbook gives a must-level expectation to define which records are eligible for a retrieval corpus, such as defined date ranges. That guidance addresses data scope for retrieval and only partly covers agent system privileges, isolation, or memory retention, so the endorsement supports the recommendation indirectly.

Neither study reported the patient population behind its test data, and both used synthetic or benchmark cases. No evidence shows whether access restrictions perform the same way for records of Medicaid, safety-net, or limited English proficiency patients, whose data may be spread across more systems.

commentary.research_gap: No study has tested least-privilege access, environment isolation, or persistent-memory access controls and retention limits for agents operating on real clinical data. Prospective evaluations in live health system deployments should measure unauthorized data access, aggregation, and retention events, along with the operational cost of maintaining permission scopes.
commentary.underserved_note: Neither the test study nor the hazard study reported population characteristics, and both used offline benchmark cases, so no test included Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Organizations serving these groups have no evidence on whether the safeguard performs equally for their patients' records.
